title: Hatshepsut's obelisk inscription dedicating it to her father Amun
summary: Luke Caverns tells of Hatshepsut's obelisk inscription dedicating it to her father Amun, about reign of Hatshepsut, c. 1470 BC at Egypt (no place named), and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: and I've read the translated hieroglyphs and she said she said um she said [clears throat] as for this obelisk it's something I'm paraphrasing but it's like as for this obelisk I erected this uh from um from electrum

plain: Luke Caverns, a researcher of ancient Egypt, says he has read translations of the carvings on an obelisk, a tall stone pillar, put up by Hatshepsut, an Egyptian ruler, at Karnak in Egypt. Paraphrasing, he says the inscription has her saying she made the obelisk from electrum, a natural mix of gold and silver, and dedicated it to her father, the god Amun. He brings it up as a clue that the ancient monuments may not be what we think.
